claims.text: The initial material consists of near-equiatomic CrMnFeCoNiCu nanoparticles.
The initial CrMnFeCoNiCu nanoparticles have a single-phase FCC structure.
The initial CrMnFeCoNiCu nanoparticles exhibit minimal elemental segregation.
An equiatomic composition maximizes configurational entropy in this HEA system.
High-temperature melt processing followed by controlled slow cooling and isothermal annealing kinetically traps the high-configurational-entropy state.
The proposed processing route preserves a single-phase FCC structure during high-temperature service.
The proposed processing route preserves a uniform elemental distribution during high-temperature service.
Controlled slow cooling limits atomic mobility.
Rapid cooling confines atoms to their high-temperature positions.
Kinetic trapping prevents the onset of elemental diffusion.
Kinetic trapping can prevent phase separation in multimetallic nanoparticles.
Slow-cooled and annealed nanoparticles will be more elementally uniform than rapidly quenched nanoparticles after service exposure.
Slow-cooled and annealed nanoparticles will retain the single FCC phase better than rapidly quenched nanoparticles.
Slow-cooled and annealed nanoparticles will maintain catalytic or thermoelectric performance better than rapidly quenched nanoparticles.
Rapidly cooled nanoparticles may exhibit enhanced segregation and phase instability during high-temperature service.
The proposed mechanism applies across 773–1173 K and 473–1923 K under inert or reducing atmospheres.
Changes in composition or processing conditions may alter phase stability and kinetic-trapping behavior.
An overly slow cooling rate may promote local elemental segregation.
Variations in isothermal annealing conditions may affect structural stability.

contradictions.description: The intervention attributes kinetic trapping to controlled slow cooling, but the mechanism states that rapid cooling confines atoms to their high-temperature positions.
The mechanism assigns position confinement to rapid cooling, while the baseline and prediction instead treat rapid quenching as the less stable, more segregated condition.
